The LENS Knowledge Base is a **living reference** maintained by members of the
[LENS Program](https://lens-program.github.io/lens-program/). It collects how identifiability,
recoverability, and related ideas are defined, formalised, and used in different fields:
statistics, econometrics, causal inference, systems biology, inverse problems, and others.

Its purpose is not just to compile what is known. By putting the different vocabularies next to
each other, we want to see where fields agree, where the same word means different things, and
**what nobody yet knows**. Those gaps become seminar topics, and eventually papers.

## What is here

- **[Concepts](concepts/index.qmd).** One page per concept. Each page holds definitions from
  several fields side by side, a formal statement, references, connections to other concepts,
  and open questions.
- **[Connections](connections.qmd).** How the concepts relate, and which terms mean roughly the
  same thing in different fields.
- **[Seminars](seminars/index.qmd).** Notes from LENS talks, each linked to the concepts it
  touched.
- **[Open problems](open-problems.qmd).** Questions raised in seminars and entries that we
  cannot yet answer.
- **[References](references.qmd).** The shared bibliography behind every citation on the site.

## Ground rules

1. **Several definitions can coexist.** A definition from another field is *added* next to
   existing ones, never written over them.
2. **Formal definitions carry citations.**
3. **Contributions are attributed** on each page.
4. **Established results are kept apart from interpretation.** Proposed connections and open
   questions are labelled as such.
5. **Nothing here is a LENS consensus** unless a page says the group discussed it and agreed.

## Contribute

Anyone in LENS can add a definition, a reference, an example, or a question. See
[How to contribute](contributing.qmd). Small suggestions can go in a
[GitHub issue](https://github.com/lens-program/knowledge-base/issues/new/choose).
